findings.title: The actual worker bootstrap executes outside the sealed exact snapshot before any worker verification
evidence: scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:1936-1993 verifies only files below snapshot_root against the exact inventory.

scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:2567-2583 constructs the worker command as sys.executable, -B, and live Path(__file__).resolve(); it does not execute a runner or bootstrap inside snapshot_root.

preexecution_seal_r5.json snapshot_static_inventory contains the legacy runner and numerical/project modules but no scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py entry. The current runner digest is only a separate seal field.

The child interpreter receives neither -I nor -S. Python startup can therefore process PYTHONPATH, sitecustomize/usercustomize, and site-package .pth code before the live runner reaches authorization or snapshot verification.

A live runner replacement after parent verification also executes before the worker can compare manifest runner_sha256 at scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:1996-2015. A self-hash after process start cannot authenticate code that has already executed.
This contradicts the r5 amendment exact_worker_inventory claim that substituted or extra code fails before any project or numerical import.
concrete_exploit_path: After the parent creates and verifies the private snapshot, alter the live runner path or supply startup code through PYTHONPATH/sitecustomize/.pth.
The supervised child starts that unsealed code under plain -B before _verify_snapshot_manifest is called.
The unsealed startup code can run arbitrary actions, bypass verification, or mutate process state before claim-bound controls become effective.
findings.impact: The sealed authority does not authenticate the first executable bytes of the actual numerical worker. Consequently r5 is not safely authorizable even though its in-process snapshot verifier is exact.
required_fix: Place the current worker runner or a minimal bootstrap in the exact sealed snapshot inventory and start that snapshot path, never live Path(__file__).

Have the parent retain a write/delete-denying held handle over the bootstrap bytes from verified copy through worker startup/import completion, or provide an equivalent race-free held-byte launch mechanism.
Invoke the worker with -I -S -B and an explicit environment allowlist; reject PYTHONPATH, user-site, .pth, sitecustomize, and usercustomize effects.
After authorization, add only individually pinned runtime package paths without processing .pth files, and verify required interpreter flags.
Recheck the exact snapshot tree and every project module immediately before and after import, before claim.

Add negative tests in which malicious PYTHONPATH/sitecustomize tries to write a marker, the live runner is swapped after parent verification, and .pyc/extra/transitive source is raced into the snapshot. All must fail before marker, import, or claim.

findings.title: Outer labels are parsed and retained before the all-fold prediction freeze
evidence: The r5 amendment outer_label_firewall requires outer truth, anomaly_type, segment targets, precision, and target-derived audits to be first accessed only after record_outer_freeze.

scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:1020-1024 calls reader.read_csv for the entire train.csv without target-free usecols. The legacy HeldSnapshotInputs parser passes the held handle to unrestricted pandas.read_csv, so label/anomaly columns are materialized before freeze.
scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:1145-1157 retains that full train DataFrame in worker state.

scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:1117-1118 calls legacy._left_censored_positive_event_counts before freeze; legacy runner:1305-1333 explicitly reads label. Although those indices are chronological training prefixes, this still disproves the package's claimed first target access chronology and leaves outer-period target columns resident and reachable.

tests/test_run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:701-781 guards only frozen_truth_oof_* state keys. It does not instrument the initial train reader or reject eager outer-period target conversion.
The numerical candidate path itself correctly moved outer interval scoring after record_outer_freeze, but the earlier reader/state path remains outside that test.
findings.impact: The promised outer evaluation firewall is structurally false: evaluation-period targets are already parsed and available in state before the candidate and all outer predictions are frozen. Intentional non-use by current functions is weaker than enforced non-access.
required_fix: Materialize the pre-freeze full training frame with target-free columns only.

Provide anchor/inner targets through a separately sealed historical-target view whose rows are physically restricted to the preregistered historical fit/inner-selection horizon and cannot contain any outer evaluation rows.
Keep all outer-period label/anomaly bytes opaque and outside the DataFrame/state API until record_outer_freeze has durably succeeded.
Remove or defer the pre-freeze label-based censor audit; if scientifically required for historical training, compute it only from the physically bounded historical-target view.
Add reader-level sentinels that fail on any pre-freeze outer-period label/anomaly conversion, indexing, column access, metric call, or target-derived audit.

findings.title: Authorization schema version and nested object membership are not enforced exactly
evidence: AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED_KEYS at runner:149-165 enforces exact top-level membership.
Parent authorization checks at runner:1692-1768 and worker checks at runner:2027-2080 do not compare authorization.schema_version with an exact expected value.
preexecution_seal and independent_qa nested objects are accessed by selected fields but their exact nested membership and complete primitive types are not validated.
findings.impact: The external digest still authenticates all bytes and critical capabilities are compared, so no immediate privilege bypass was demonstrated. However the stated exact fail-closed authorization schema is looser than implemented and forward/unknown fields could be silently accepted in nested objects.
required_fix: Enforce an exact authorization schema_version constant in parent and worker.
Enforce exact nested key sets and primitive types for preexecution_seal and independent_qa.
Add wrong-version, missing/extra nested field, and wrong-type negative tests that fail before snapshot, import, repository mutation, or claim.
